subject: MerchantX ServeFlow discovery — qualification, POC scope & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@merchantx.com>, Samir Desai <samir@merchantx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: MerchantX ServeFlow discovery — qualification, POC scope & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our side and suggested next steps. I tried to capture the pain, goals, and the technical asks we discussed so we have a shared starting point.

Key pain points you called out:
- Large latency spikes during daytime peak (checkout flows) leading to timeouts for assistant-driven upsell paths.
- High per-request cost from current pipeline (embeddings + rerank + gen) that scales poorly with volume.
- Need to unify streaming responses with function-calling so UI can progressively render while ops call downstream services.

Goals we heard:
1) Reduce median inference latency for decisioning path to <200ms for 512-token windows.
2) Cut cost per completed user flow by ~30% via batching/caching and model selection.
3) Deliver a prototype that demonstrates embedding-based product search + rerank + streamed answer generation with structured JSON outputs for downstream billing.

Technical asks / requirements you mentioned:
- Support for streaming token responses and function calling in the same session (client must be able to receive partial text and then a structured function call).
- SDKs for Node + Go with native streaming helpers and clear examples for KV caching.
- Ability to pin model version and fallback policy for peak hours; quantization recommendations welcome.
- SOC2 / audit log evidence and data residency in us-west for PII workloads.

Proposed POC scope (high level)
- 2-week technical POC: integrate Redwood SDK with your product-search service: embeddings -> rerank -> stream gen.
- Deliverables: sample app + replay test harness, latency and cost dashboard, and a short runbook outlining fallback policies.

Immediate next steps
1) Karthik to send a short POC scope doc (engineering checklist + infra needs) — by EOD tomorrow.
2) Marissa to share a commercial sketch for trial capacity and pricing guardrails.
3) We schedule a 60-min engineering scoping call next week (proposed slots on calendar link below).
4) You to share a short dataset sample for embeddings to validate cost/latency estimates (anonymized).

Attachments: redwood-sdks-compat-matrix.pdf, merchantx-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Irene
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173

From: Emily Park <emily@merchantx.com>

Subject: Re: MerchantX ServeFlow discovery — qualification, POC scope & next steps

Irene — thanks for the thorough recap, this lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Timeline: We are targeting a vendor evaluation window of Nov 15–Dec 10 with a pilot to start by mid-December if things look good. Will that timeline work for Redwood?

2) Procurement: procurement will need a cost cap for the pilot and an estimate for expected token costs at our projected QPS (I can share numbers after this email).

3) Security/residency: SOC2 is required. Also, for the pilot we need logs and audit events to remain in us-west-2. Can you confirm how Redwood supports that for a POC?

4) Technical: the key thing is the streaming+function-call UX. We want to ensure the client receives partial text updates while a function call is being prepared and then the structured output (JSON) sent to our service to execute. If you have a short example snippet for Node showing streaming -> function call -> structured output that would be helpful.

We're happy to provide an anonymized dataset sample for embeddings. I'll coordinate internally and send that by Friday.

Proposed time for the scoping call: Mon Nov 9 10:00am PT or Tue Nov 10 2:00pm PT — any preference?

Thanks — Emily
Emily Park
Head of Product, ServeFlow | MerchantX
emily@merchantx.com

Subject: RE: MerchantX ServeFlow discovery — POC engineering notes

Irene / Marissa — quick engineering line-items to include in the POC scope doc (attached poc-scope.md). Notes below are targeted to make the scoping call efficient.

POC engineering checklist (high-level)
- Ingress pattern: ingestion via streaming websocket -> tokenized request pipeline. We'll use continuous batching with a 25ms max hold window to reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs.
- Streaming + function call: implement the Redwood streaming client with earlyText callbacks and then a terminal function_call event that returns a structured JSON payload. We'll provide a Node example: stream.on('token', cb) then stream.on('function_call', cb) — the handler will call your product API.
- Embeddings + rerank: run a hybrid approach — coarse candidate retrieval using approximate NN on embeddings (64-d reduced), then a lightweight reranker model (quantized 4-bit) to preserve quality while lowering cost.
- Pin & fallback policy: ability to pin stable-medium model for peak hours; fallback to distilled-low-cost variant when queueing exceeds threshold.
- Data residency: deploy a private, short-lived endpoint in us-west-2 for the POC to ensure logs and audit events stay in-region. We'll coordinate with infra for VPN whitelisting.

Infra needs from MerchantX
- Sample dataset for embeddings (anonymized) and a representative QPS profile for peak and off-peak.
- Test account access for your product API to validate function calls (sandbox).

Deliverables (2-week POC)
- Working integration + sample app, latency/cost dashboard, runbook for fallback, simple perf report.

I'll attach poc-scope.md with more detail. Happy to refine during the scoping call.

-Karthik
